speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned sudden-onset vertigo; to help narrow down the cause, how long has this spinning sensation been happening, and did it start while you were walking, turning your head, or lying down?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms lasting exactly 3 minutes and resolving while you were lying down are very specific; did you notice any other neurological symptoms like double vision, slurred speech, or weakness in your limbs during that episode? Also, do you have a history of high blood pressure or heart disease?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical presentation of sudden-onset vertigo lasting exactly three minutes, triggered by lying down, and the complete resolution of symptoms at baseline are classic for BPPV. No further imaging or laboratory tests are required for this diagnosis.
